outcomes: Predicts how the count changes when a defender is added, the front piece is pinned or the rear piece is missing
Verifies a capture sequence square by square before playing the first capture
Says which changes to a position leave the count as it was

steps.text:
This lesson follows **X-ray and batteries: the piece behind joins in** and **X-ray: count every piece on the line**. Here the count is not given; you predict it after a change.
Start from a battery that wins. Change one thing: a defender arrives, the front piece becomes pinned, or the rear piece leaves the line. Predict whether the count still wins, then check it square by square.

**Three changes that matter:** a new defender of the target square; a front piece pinned to its king, so it cannot capture and the rear piece never joins in; a rear piece that no longer stands on the line.
**A change that does not matter:** a move that touches neither the line nor the target. **Rule of thumb:** recount after every change; never carry the old count over.

steps.title: Same battery, one change
steps.prompt: Black to move: does the first rook capture on the e-file win a rook? One change each time. Predict, then check.
Write the three changes from this lesson on paper. For one game position of your own with two rooks on a file, predict what each change would do to the count, then check one of them.

steps.text: **Remember.** A winning battery can change, so recount after every change. Three changes matter: a new defender of the target square, a front piece pinned so the rear piece never joins in, and a rear piece that leaves the line. A move that touches neither the line nor the target does not matter. Never carry the old count over.
